discovery.none: Manual selection only. Local names vary widely by pack vendor and the shared FF00/FF01/FF02 endpoint is also used by Bluetti, so no advertised signal is a safe automatic JBD identity match. After the user selects a candidate, require a valid, fully reassembled and checksummed 0xDD ... 0x77 response to the read-only 0x03 basic-info request before treating it as JBD or offering any write.

device.manufacturer: Shenzhen Jiabaida (JBD) — many LiFePO4 pack rebrands (Overkill Solar, LIONTRON, ECO-WORTHY, ...)
device.name: JBD / Xiaoxiang Smart BMS
device.notes:
JBD (a.k.a. Xiaoxiang) smart battery-management systems ship inside a huge number of LiFePO4/Li-ion packs under many brands. The same frames run over a plug-in BLE module or a UART (9600 8N1). No cloud; read telemetry and, in factory (EEPROM) mode, write protection settings and toggle the charge/ discharge FETs and balancer.
GATT: service 0000ff00-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb; notify (RX) 0000ff01-...; write (TX) 0000ff02-....
FRAME: start 0xDD, then payload, a 2-byte big-endian checksum, end 0x77. Command byte 0xA5 = read, 0x5A = write. Request checksum = 0x10000 - sum(register + length + data), excluding DD, A5, the checksum itself and 77. Response checksum = 0x10000 - sum(register + status + length + data), excluding DD, the checksum and 77. The vectors DD A5 03 00 FF FD 77, DD A5 04 00 FF FC 77 and DD A5 05 00 FF FB 77 prove that A5 is outside the request sum.
RESPONSE REASSEMBLY: notifications may split a frame anywhere. Starting at DD, read register, status and length, then accumulate to exactly 4 + length + 3 bytes total (four header bytes, data, two checksum bytes and 77) before validating the terminator and checksum. Never CRC individual notifications or parse a partial response.
KEY REGISTERS:
  0x03 basic info — pack voltage (u16 BE @0, 10 mV), current (s16 BE @2,
       negative = discharge), remaining capacity (u16 BE @4) and design
       capacity (u16 BE @6), cycle count, protection/error flags, software
       version, SOC %, FET status bits (charge/discharge), cell count,
       NTC count + temps (0.1 K). Offsets are into the response payload,
       which starts after DD/register/status/length. operation_status is
       payload byte 20 (whole-frame byte 24). On firmware implementing its
       bit 7 as the units flag, set means current 100 mA and both
       capacities 100 mAh; otherwise current is 10 mA and both capacities
       10 mAh. Do not generalize one scale across firmware.
  0x04 per-cell voltages (u16 @ 1 mV)
  0x05 device name string
EEPROM config needs factory mode: write 0x56 0x78 to register 0x00; exit via register 0x01. Control registers: 0xE1 MOSFET control (bit0 disable charge FET, bit1 disable discharge FET), 0xE2 balancer control.
Newer firmware may add an authentication exchange (frames starting FF AA ... 77) and a 6-byte password (since firmware 0x16).

openness.notes: Not officially published; the register map was reverse-engineered by the community and multiple implementations agree. The newer-firmware auth handshake internals are the least-settled part.

upstream_docs.covers: The full register map, 0xDD/0x77 framing, checksum, and EEPROM config registers.
upstream_docs.title: bms-tools — JBD register map

credentials.notes: No pairing on older firmware; newer firmware may require an authentication exchange and/or a password before writes. Reads are unauthenticated. SAFETY: writing FET-control or protection registers on a live pack is dangerous — treat writes as advanced.

factory_reset.description:
The reason anyone needs this is almost always the same: somebody set a Bluetooth password in the Xiaoxiang app and is now locked out, because that app has no function to remove one. Two escape routes exist and both leave the app behind. JBD's own desktop tool includes a password-clearing function, and the open BMS-Tools desktop application can send a password-reset command; either way a USB communication module is needed, not Bluetooth.
A full factory restore via button presses on the PCB itself is also described by the community, but no reliable sequence was established here — hence low confidence and no steps for it. On a device whose parameters decide whether a lithium pack is protected, a guessed button sequence is not something to publish.
SAFETY: after any restore, verify the cell count, capacity and every protection threshold before reconnecting the pack.
factory_reset.effect: A firmware-level restore returns the BMS to factory defaults, including clearing a Bluetooth password that has been set. Cell configuration and protection parameters go with it — on a battery management system those are safety settings, so this is not a casual operation.

procedures.basis: JBD's desktop tool and the open BMS-Tools application, both documented by the Xiaoxiang/Overkill Solar community as the way out of a password lockout. Requires a USB communication module.
procedures.name: Clear the Bluetooth password over USB

steps.action: Connect a USB communication module to the BMS's UART port.
From JBD's desktop tool or BMS-Tools, issue the password clear / password reset command.
steps.expect: The Bluetooth password is removed and the app connects again.

methods.description: Manually select the candidate, connect and subscribe to notify char 0xFF01. Prove JBD identity with the read-only, checksummed 0x03 exchange before offering 0x04 reads or any write; FF00 alone is not enough because Bluetti shares the endpoint.

steps.action: Manually select the BMS candidate; do not auto-identify from service 0xFF00. Connect and subscribe to the notify characteristic (0xFF01).
Write the exact 0x03 read DD A5 03 00 FF FD 77 to 0xFF02; reassemble to 4 + length + 3 bytes, then validate terminator 0x77 and the response checksum before parsing basic info or offering writes.
steps.expect: A valid 0xDD-framed 0x03 response with status 0x00 and checksum over register + status + length + data confirms the JBD protocol rather than a shared-endpoint lookalike.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision: connect over BLE, subscribe to the notify characteristic, and write 0xDD-framed read/write commands. Confidence high: the register map is exhaustive and several implementations agree.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; a new BLE client connects independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The GATT service/char UUIDs, the 0xDD/0x77 framing, command bytes and register map are from the bms-tools register map and syssi/esphome-jbd-bms / kolins-cz.

entities.name: Pack Current
entities.notes: Signed BE at payload offset 2. Operation-status at payload offset 20 (whole-frame byte 24), bit 7 selects 100 mA on firmware implementing that flag; otherwise 10 mA. Unsigned BE capacities at offsets 4/6 use corresponding 100/10 mAh.

design_capacity.signedness: unsigned; unit scale selected by operation_status bit 7

pack_current.signedness: signed; negative = discharge; unit scale selected by operation_status bit 7

remaining_capacity.signedness: unsigned; unit scale selected by operation_status bit 7

basic_info_response.fixture_padding: 12 zero bytes at payload offsets 8-19, then operation_status at payload offset 20 (whole-frame byte 24).
basic_info_response.payload_basis: Response payload begins after DD, register, status and length, so whole-frame offset = payload offset + 4.
basic_info_response.unit_selection: operation_status bit 7 clear: current 10 mA and capacities 10 mAh. Set on firmware implementing the flag: current 100 mA and capacities 100 mAh. Do not apply one scale to all firmware.

characteristics.name: Notify (RX)
characteristics.notes: Responses arrive fragmented here. Reassemble to 4 + length + 3 bytes, then validate the 0x77 terminator and checksum over register + status + length + data before parsing.

read_basic_info.description: Read register 0x03 (pack voltage, current, SOC, FET status, temps, flags). Frame: DD A5 03 00 FF FD 77.

read_cell_voltages.description: Read register 0x04 (per-cell voltages, u16 @ 1 mV). Frame: DD A5 04 00 FF FC 77.

read_device_name.description: Read register 0x05 (device name string). Frame: DD A5 05 00 FF FB 77.

services.name: JBD BMS service
services.notes: Notify (RX) on 0xFF01, write (TX) on 0xFF02. These endpoints are shared with Bluetti, not an identity. Requests checksum register+length+data; responses checksum register+status+length+data, in both cases excluding DD, the checksum and 77 (and excluding A5 on requests).
